title: Goal Encoding in LLMs
abstract: arXiv:2611.17297v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: We investigate whether and how LLMs encode goals: internal neural representations that precede and guide action, and that are flexible enough to be realized through many different execution paths. We construct a coding setting with multiple sub-tasks that allows us to evaluate goal-seeking behavior and the selection of sub-goals. In this setting, we localize an encoding of the next sub-goal in the outputs of a sparse set of attention heads. The same heads can be used to decode the LM's future actions in natural language (e.g., "I'm checking if a word is a palindrome"). We verify that this encoding is causal for next action and is plastic: transplanting it into a different environment, e.g., another programming language, triggers the same operation realized with a different sequence of tokens. translated_abstract: 我们研究LLM是否以及如何编码目标：即先于行动出现并引导行动的内部神经表征，这些表征足够灵活，能够通过许多不同的执行路径来实现。我们构建了一个包含多个子任务的编程环境，使我们能够评估目标寻求行为以及子目标的选择。在这一环境中，我们将下一个子目标的编码定位在稀疏的一组注意力头的输出中。同样的注意力头还可以用来以自然语言解码语言模型的未来行动（例如，“我正在检查一个词是否是回文”）。我们验证了这种编码对下一个行动具有因果性，并且具有可塑性：将其移植到不同的环境中（例如另一种编程语言），会触发相同的操作，但通过不同的token序列来实现。语言模型还在整个行动执行过程中持续维持这种编码，这一点令人费解，因为没有循环机制的transformer语言模型无法携带……（原文摘要在此处被截断）
tldr: 该研究在LLM中定位到编码下一子目标的稀疏注意力头集合，证明这种目标表征对后续行动具有因果性、可跨环境灵活迁移，并在整个行动执行过程中被持续维持。
en_tdlr: This work localizes a sparse set of attention heads in LLMs that encode the next sub-goal, showing this representation is causal for subsequent actions, plastically transferable across environments, and sustained throughout action execution.
